DEFINITIONS
ISO 50001:2018
EN ISO 50001:2018 is the international standard for energy management.
DEC
A Display Energy Certificate (DEC) shows the energy performance of a 
building based on actual energy consumption recorded over the last 12 
months. It compares the actual energy use against the energy use for a 
benchmark building of the same type. Similar to a domestic Building Energy 
Rating (BER), DECs are displayed on a scale from A to G, with an A rating being 
the most efficient and a G rating being the least efficient.
Climate Action 
and Low Carbon 
Development 
(Amendment) Act 
2021
Climate Action and Low Carbon Development (Amendment) Act 2021, 
supports Ireland’s transition to Net Zero and to achieve a 51% reduction in 
overall greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 and setting Ireland on a path to 
reach net-zero emissions by no later than 2050. It establishes a legally binding 
framework with clear targets and commitments to ensure Ireland achieves 
national, EU and international climate goals and obligations in the near and 
long term. The Act mandates the development of a comprehensive Climate 
Action Plan, which must be updated annually.

Decarbonisation
Decarbonisation is the removal or reduction of carbon dioxide inputs from 
human activity into the atmosphere which is important for limiting global 
warming. The main levers for decarbonisation are the development of 
renewable energies, switching fuels and the improvement of energy efficiency.
EE
Energy Efficiency (EE) is using less energy to complete the same task. 
Retrofitting options can be used to reduce energy usage. These may include 
switching to LED lighting and energy efficient appliances or upgrading 
insulation. Energy efficiency has a variety of benefits including reducing GHG 
emissions, reducing demand for energy imports, and lowering energy costs.
EEDPP
Energy Efficiency and Decarbonisation Pathfinder Programme is co-funded 
by Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and 
Science (DFHERIS) and the Department of the Environment, Climate and 
Communications (DECC) through the SEAI and administered by the Higher 
Education Authority. 
GPP
Green Public Procurement (GPP), or Sustainable Procurement, is a process 
where public authorities seek to source goods, services or works with a 
reduced environmental impact.
Triple E Register
List of energy efficient products. Products on this register all meet a minimum 
set of stringent energy efficiency criteria and typically will be of a best-in-
class efficiency standard.
Register of 
Opportunities 
(ROO)
Register of Opportunities (ROO) is a list of energy efficiency opportunities 
developed as part of an energy management system.
GTT Model
The Gap-to-Target model (GtT model) is a spreadsheet model for use by 
public bodies to evaluate their energy efficiency (EE) performance and 
energy-related greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions over time, using data and 
methodologies from SEAI’s Public Sector Monitoring and Reporting (M&R) 
system
CAM
The Public Sector Climate Action Mandate (CAM) highlights the main climate 
action objectives for public bodies and will be reviewed annually. 
SEAI
The SEAI is Ireland’s national sustainable energy authority and works with 
householders, businesses, communities, and government to create a cleaner 
energy future.

FOREWORD
The centrality of 
Sustainability in 
the everyday life 
of the South East 
Technological University 
(SETU) is underpinned 
by our inaugural Strategic Plan 2024-
2028 ‘Connecting for Impact’. Through 
the articulation of our vision: ‘SETU 
will be a leading global technological 
University with transformative impact 
on our community, the south east of 
Ireland and beyond’ to definition of our 
Mission that ‘SETU is an international, 
entrepreneurial and connected multi-
campus Technological University 
that will drive sustainable economic, 
environmental, cultural and social 
development in the south east of Ireland’, 
to the clear statement in our Values that 
‘We act sustainably, responsibly and 
ethically’, SETU is committed to delivering 
and leading in this vital area.
Our strategic plan commits us to 
ensuring that sustainable development 
is embedded in all we do. Manifesting 
in the resourcing of a key leadership 
role – our Associate Vice-President for 
Sustainability- and the establishment of 
The Sustainable Development Office to 
drive activity in this domain including our 
Climate Action Lead, SETU is dedicated to 
shaping a sustainable future. Our climate 
action roadmap builds upon the legacy of 
paving the way, marking SETU as a leading 
university in our effort to protect our 
environment and society.
This SETU Climate Action Roadmap (CAR) 
sets out the University’s plans to reduce 
emissions and meet decarbonisation 
and energy efficiency targets. The CAR 
has been prepared in accordance with 
guidance from the Sustainable Energy 
Authority of Ireland (SEAI) and the Climate 
Action and Low Carbon Development 
(Amendment) Act 2021. Subsequent 
measures and goals for the public sector 
are set out in the Climate Action Plan 
(CAP) as part of the annually updated 
Public Sector Climate Action Mandate 
2025. 
Through our CAR and the related activity, 
we are ensuring sustainable development 
is embedded in SETU’s leadership, 
governance and operations, and that the 
SETU community of staff and students 
are sustainably aware and incorporating 
sustainable practice into daily University 
life.
David Denieffe
Chief Operations and Energy Performance 
Officer at SETU, October 2025

1.2	 IMPROVE ENERGY EFFICIENCY IN THE PUBLIC SECTOR BY 50% BY 2030.
SETU is currently on track to achieve the 
energy efficiency target of 50% by 2030 
compared to a 2006 to 2008 baseline, 
(please see figure 6 below). SETU will meet 
2030 energy efficiency targets by:
•	 improving operations of the university 
through the use of certified energy 
management systems such as ISO50001;
•	 unlocking the potential of our buildings 
through smart, sustainable space 
optimisation; 
•	 planned investment in existing buildings 
to improve efficiency – for building 
refurbishments and deep retrofits a 
minimum target of BER B or better is 
set which will deliver significant carbon 
savings as both fabric and plant are 
upgraded through EEDPP; 
•	 designing all new buildings to near-
zero energy building standard with BER 
A and energy efficiency design (EED) 
techniques incorporated and 
•	 enhancing and expanding current energy 
awareness programmes and establishing 
further measures to promote individual 
behavioural change through energy 
awareness campaigns and staff and 
student training.

2.1	 LEADERSHIP AND GOVERNANCE FOR CLIMATE ACTION
As per the University’s strategic plan, 
SETU is committed to ensuring that 
‘sustainable development is embedded 
in SETU’s leadership, governance and 
operations, and the SETU community 
of staff and students are sustainably 
aware and incorporate sustainable 
practice into their daily University life’. 
In 2024, SETU appointed an Associate 
Vice President for Sustainability 
(AVPS), Dr David Ryan, and the 
Sustainable Development Office 
(SDO) was established at the 
University, please see figure 7 below. 
The AVPS acts as SETU Climate 
and Sustainability Champion with 
responsibility for implementation and 
reporting on the requirements set 
out in the SEAI Public Sector Climate 
Action Mandate. 
The SDO is preparing to publish 
a Sustainability Strategy for the 
University, with Climate Action as a 
core pillar. Stakeholder consultation 
is ongoing and the strategy will be 
published in the 2025/2026 academic 
year.
As per the Public Sector Energy 
Strategy, the role of Energy 
Performance Officer (EPO) has 
transferred from the Vice President 
of Corporate Affairs to the Chief 
Operations Officer (COO) in September 
2025 with the appropriate training 
provided. Oversight and monitoring 
of the SETU Climate Action Roadmap 
continues to be a priority for the 
President, Executive Management 
Team (EMT) and the University 
Governing Body. Figure 8 outlines the 
leadership and governance structure 
in place to ensure synergy between 
the University’s broader climate action, 
the University’s strategic plan and 
Sustainability Strategy. 
SETU have established an Energy 
Team comprising of Significant Energy 
Users (SEU’s) across the University. 
The purpose of the energy team is to 
lead and advise on: 
• improving energy efficiency by at 
least 50% by 2030; 
• reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) 
emissions by at least 51% by 2030 
and planning for 2050 targets; 
• embedding energy efficiency into 
operations; 
• raising energy awareness across 
SETU communities.
The roles, responsibilities and terms 
of reference of the Energy Team are 
included in Appendix 1 and 2.

The University has committed to not 
installing heating systems that use fossil 
fuels after 2023 in: 
a)	 new buildings, and 
b)	 “Major renovation” retrofit projects as 
defined in the Energy Performance of 
Buildings Directive (EPBD) unless at 
least one of the following exceptions 
applies: 
•	 The fossil-fuel use is only through 
using electricity from the grid. 
•	 There is no technically viable non-
fossil alternative (generally only 
related to applications for a purpose 
other than space heating). 
•	 The installation of a renewable space 
heating system would increase final 
CO2 emissions. 
•	 The fossil-fuel use is provided for 
backup, peaking, or operational 
purposes (and makes up less than 
10% of annual heating energy). 
•	 Where the direct replacement of 
existing fossil fuel heating is required 
for an emergency maintenance 
purpose. 
SETU understand the need to reduce the 
reliance on burning fossil fuels to provide 
heat to the current buildings and will 
pursue all avenues to decarbonise legacy 
heating systems in all the existing buildings, 
as part of any renovation/upgrade works. 
This will include a proposed program to 
replace the existing fossil fuelled heating 
systems with more sustainable options 
such as electric powered heat pumps and 
renewables.

works to achieve <5³/hr/m² @50pa

lighting 
•	 Installation of energy efficient Air 
Handling Units and associated controls
•	 BER B rating achieved.

INTRODUCTION 
The Sustainable Development Office 
(SDO) of South East Technological 
University (SETU) has established an 
Energy Committee. The committee 
shall be known as the Energy Team.
The SETU Strategic Plan ‘Connecting 
for Impact’ sets out a vision for SETU 
to ‘be a leading global technological 
University with transformative impact 
on our community, the south east 
of Ireland and beyond’ and commits 
the university to ensuring that 
‘sustainable development is embedded 
in SETU’s leadership, governance 
and operations, and that the SETU 
community of staff and students are 
sustainably aware and incorporate 
sustainable practice into daily 
university life’. (Strategic Objective 9). 
SETU established the office for 
Sustainable Development in May 
2024 and appointed its first Associate 
Vice President for Sustainability. The 
inaugural SETU Sustainability strategy 
intends that SETU be a model of 
sustainable development, leading 
by example and by influence while 
showcasing a vision for a sustainable 
world. The plan is structured around 
four priority areas namely:
•	 Climate: Net zero 2040. Foster a 
culture of climate action, minimise 
our carbon footprint, and establish 
SETU campuses as living laboratory 
spaces for green and sustainable 
technologies and solutions.
•	 Nature: People and nature centred 
campus spaces. Enhance, protect 
and restore biodiversity across our 
campuses, champion green spaces, 
embed nature-positive practices 
into operations, and position SETU 
as a living landscape for learning, 
innovation, nature restoration and 
community engagement.
•	 Education: Sustainable development 
in teaching, learning, research and 
engagement. Integrate an Education 
for Sustainable Development 
approach into our teaching, 
learning, research and engagement 
across all disciplines, equipping 
our students with the knowledge 
and skills to navigate a complex 
and rapidly evolving world, and 
empowering our graduates to both 
embody sustainability and embrace 
the opportunities it offers in their 
careers and in their daily lives.
•	 Impact: Regional action for global 
challenges. Lead by example, 
influence and impact and strengthen 
cohesive, sustainability-focused 
and locally informed, strategic 
partnerships to drive integrated 
socioeconomic and environmental 
development across the South East.
